title: Investigation Manual
claim: Three golden checks: Source - Evidence - Context.
summary: Always verify who wrote a claim (Source), what supports it (Evidence), and whether details or dates were removed (Context).

title: Alex's Letter
claim: VitaPulse is selling everyone's private medical information!
summary: Contains a blog URL and a highlighted accusation that VitaPulse secretly sells medical records. Unlocks the blog on the office computer.

title: Unverified Blog Claim
claim: All medical records are secretly being sold.
summary: Unidentified author, no traceable supporting sources, and a definitive headline that goes beyond what VitaPulse's privacy policy actually states.

title: VitaPulse Privacy Policy - Section 4.2
claim: Some information may be shared with third-party partners.
summary: Raises a legitimate privacy question about scope and purpose of third-party sharing, though it does not by itself prove secret sales of all medical records.

title: VitaPulse Promotional Agreement
claim: The viral video influencer has a paid promotional relationship with VitaPulse.
summary: Commercial sponsorship is relevant when judging the video's independence; popularity alone is not proof of clinical effectiveness.

title: Privacy Permissions Corrected
claim: Sofia selected Allow All (health data, contacts, location, microphone).
summary: A personal health diary only needs explicitly chosen health records; contacts, continuous precise location, and microphone should be turned off.

title: Viral Video - Hospital Endorsement Claim
claim: Viral video displays a hospital logo and implies official endorsement.
source: Viral Video: Doctors Missed It, But VitaPulse Saved My Life!
summary: A logo in a viral video does not prove official hospital involvement; it must be verified against official health sources.

title: Official Clinical Evidence Guidance
claim: Clinical claims for digital health apps require suitable scientific evidence.
summary: Official public guidance shows no clinical approval or validated early-detection performance for VitaPulse.

title: Altered Approval Screenshot
claim: VitaPulse Is Officially Approved for Early Disease Detection.
source: Daniel's Screenshot vs Official Portal Comparison
summary: Omits the document's date and context and inserts approval wording absent from the original official portal page.
